fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The man measures the room next to the inner sanctuary at twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide, and then he says to Ezekiel, "This is the Most Holy Place." (Ezekiel 41:4) Notice it's a perfect square. I like a tidy room.

The ark is a famous name, so I see why it jumped out. But this verse never mentions it. What the man says about the wooden altar is, "This is the table that is before the LORD." (Ezekiel 41:22) The ark isn't named anywhere in this passage.

Elders are a good guess, but this verse isn't about them. The man says these are the holy chambers where "…the priests who approach the LORD will eat the most holy offerings." (Ezekiel 42:13) The word is priests, friend. Nobody else gets named for these chambers.

Levites are a good guess, friend, but they aren't in this verse. The man says the priests put on other clothes "…before they approach the places that are for the people." (Ezekiel 42:14) The word is people. The man doesn't name anybody else.

A prince is a fancy guess, but this verse says something plainer. The priests put on other clothes "…before they approach the places that are for the people." (Ezekiel 42:14) People is the word, baker.
